## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `17988ade2c9a3e191a12c51a7419669c612ce2a5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0015-external-datasource-federation.md, docs/adr/0062-external-datasource-runtime.md, skills/objectstack-data/rules/datasources.md + packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-env-credential.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-connection-service.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-admin-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-admin-service.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-credential-migration.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/default-datasource-driver-factory.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/dev.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/datasource-env-credentials-default.ts, packages/runtime/src/default-datasource-plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/declared-datasources.ts, packages/spec/src/data/driver/common.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/datasource.zod.ts, packages/drivers/driver-odata/src/plugin.ts, packages/drivers/driver-odata/src/odata-driver.ts, skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-data/references/_index.md, skills/objectstack-data/evals/hooks-security-seeds-datasources.json, .changeset/28209-skills-code-datasource-env-credential.md, scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs, packages/skills/scripts/sync-catalog.mjs, AGENTS.md

Face: governed rules text (`skills/**` ×1, `docs/adr/**` ×2; 3 of 3 governed paths). The diff is prose only — no schema, export, key, value, error code or runtime line moves — so the review is whether each taught sentence matches how `main` (merge-base `5da3a8ce`, and no commit since has touched the cited code) resolves a credential for a datasource declared in code against one saved through Setup. Every claim below was read in the cited code with `git show`; nothing was built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

**Acceptance set and public faces: unchanged.** No `packages/spec` path, no `exports`, no `.d.ts`. `Clause-②: no` on the PR body and the changeset is correct. The published surface that does move is `@objectstack/skills` (`skills/**` is copied by `sync-catalog.mjs` into `dist/skills`, the package's only `files` entry besides README/CHANGELOG), so the derived judgments are the taught sentences, one by one.

**`skills/objectstack-data/rules/datasources.md`, "Credentials — fail-closed" — each sentence against `main`:**

- "A code-declared datasource reads one at connect from `OS_DATASOURCE_{NAME}_PASSWORD` (`NAME` = the name upper-cased)" — correct. `datasourceEnvCredentialVar` is `OS_DATASOURCE_` + `name.toUpperCase().replace(/[^A-Z0-9]/g, '_')` + `_PASSWORD`; the schema name regex is `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$` (`datasource.zod.ts`), on which "upper-cased" is the whole rule (the only non-alphanumeric a valid name can carry is `_`, mapped to itself). The slot is consulted only on a `declared-auto` connect whose name is in the host's `code-datasource-names` set and that is not `asDefault` (`envCredentialVarFor`; the `!opts.asDefault` guard) — i.e. exactly the boot connect the authoring agent's datasource meets.
- "while the host switch `OS_DATASOURCE_ENV_CREDENTIALS` is `on` (`os serve`/`start`/`dev` default it on; a library composition is off; `on`/`off` only)" — correct. `resolveDatasourceEnvCredentialsSwitch`: unset/empty ⇒ off, `on`/`off` case-insensitive, anything else throws; `DatasourceAdminServicePlugin.init()` calls it and spreads `envCredentials` only when true, so a bad value refuses the boot. `serve.ts` calls `stampDatasourceEnvCredentialsDefault(process.env, …)` before the admin plugin is built (stamps `on` only when unset/empty); `start.ts` and `dev.ts` spawn `serve`. `DatasourceConnectionServiceConfig.envCredentials` is optional and absent by default, so a composition that never runs that line is off.
- "Operator caution: an installed package may declare a datasource of any free name and so read that variable" — correct and stated as a caution, no recipe. `declared-datasources.ts` calls `contributeCodeDatasourceNames(ctx, names)` for an installed package's datasources, so under `os serve` they are in the set `isCodeDatasource` reads.
- "`external` may instead name one channel, which wins and never falls back to the variable" — correct. The slot sits in `connect()` under `if (!credentialsRef && connector === undefined && !opts.asDefault)`, after the fail-closed `credentialsRef` resolution and the D7 connector borrow, each of which returns `failed-credentials` before the slot is reached.
- The kept `credentialsRef` / `connector` bullets and the fail-closed paragraph are unchanged text, still true on `main`.

**The five deletions, each with a home (the ratchet payment):** the `datasource.zod.ts` pointer — `references/_index.md:12`; "(default: `'default'`)" — `SKILL.md` field table row `datasource`; `// writable: true` and "Otherwise every write … is rejected." — the Writes section's two-gate sentence still states the rule; the "Column mapping" ✅ bullet — the example's `columnMap` line shows the key and its direction, and the ❌ `field.columnName` rule stays; "(at `defineStack`, else at connect)" and "and its federated objects registered," — timing clauses whose rule survives in the sentence they hung on. No rule lost; no line re-wrapped to gain room.

**ADR-0015 — the Amended-by entry, the D7 inline correction, the §10 bullet and the §10 note:**

- Form: the header already lists four amendments in the same "`#NNNN` (date, ruling) — scope — see the note" shape; the new entry matches. The `Status` line stays `Accepted` — correct, the amendment narrows nothing and neither ADR is superseded (ADR-0062 "supersedes the runtime portions of ADR-0015 §18" only, and names ADR-0015 as the canonical binding decision; the PR keeps that split: the operator caution lives in 0015 §10, 0062 D3 points to it). The §10 note uses the blockquote-with-bold-lede form of the three existing notes; the inline `*(Amended …)*` on the bullet copies the D7 precedent on the same bullet.
- Facts: variable derivation and example — verified above. "the password for `postgres`, `mysql` and `mongodb`, the `authToken` for `turso`" — `default-datasource-driver-factory.ts` maps `spec.secret` to `password` in the pg, mysql and mongo arms; the migration table in `datasource-credential-migration.ts` records turso's slot as `authToken`, read from `spec.secret`. Switch semantics, `init()` refusal, `os serve` stamp, `start`/`dev` — verified. "never a record's `origin`" — `servedOrigin` and `envCredentialVarFor` both read the provenance set only. "`default` keeps `OS_DATABASE_URL` (an `asDefault` connect never reads the slot)" — the guard. Failure text — verbatim with `main`: the driver's `errMsg(err)` followed by ` (note: datasource 'NAME' is defined in code and reads its credential from OS_DATASOURCE_NAME_PASSWORD at connect, which is not set on this host)`, verdict `failed-degraded`. Collision — the second connect is refused `failed-credentials` with the message naming both datasources and the variable, before `read`; a failed attempt deletes its `claimedVariable`. "Setup → Datasources form refuses a code-origin datasource, and nothing else mints one" — the create door throws `a code-defined datasource owns this name (read-only)`, the credential-migration door refuses `origin !== 'runtime'`, and the saved-datasource Test door probes without the connection service, so no door binds a handle for a code datasource. Spec sentence — `CODE_DEFINED_CREDENTIAL_ROUTE` is appended at five refusal prescriptions and the `password` key description in `common.zod.ts` and the two `password` guidance entries in `datasource.zod.ts`: 5 + 1 + 2, as the note says. "Not taken" — matches the guard list in `datasource-env-credential.ts`'s own header.
- One loose word, not a must-fix: "A plugin driver that resolves its credential per request (the OData driver resolves `credentialsRef` that way)". `driver-odata/plugin.ts` resolves the handle at the first request and again on a 401, not on every request. The operative claim — the OData driver never consumes `spec.secret`, so the slot cannot feed it — holds (`plugin.ts` reads only the secret store or the connector handle).

**ADR-0062 D3 amendment:** the five conditions (neither channel declared, not `asDefault`, trigger `declared-auto`, name in the code set, host opted in) are the exact predicate of `connect()` plus `envCredentialVarFor`. The sentence "**Default behavior** below gains one line: …" declares the growth in the note without editing the normative list — the same form the ADR's `#4462` amendment used ("The D2 gate grows (d)" while the D2 paragraph still lists (a)–(c)); consistent with precedent, and the PR body says the normative bullets were left alone on purpose.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/skills` **patch** — correct, and the changeset is owed. `skills/**` ships in `@objectstack/skills` (`dist/skills`, produced by `sync-catalog.mjs`, listed in `files`), so AGENTS.md's Post-Task Checklist item 3 applies ("⛔ never `skip-changeset`: that label is for a diff that publishes nothing from any released package") and `scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs` says the same in its failure text ("a skills/** change does: it ships in @objectstack/skills"). The order's `skip-changeset` line was wrong on this point; the dev named the deviation rather than following it, which is what `os-dev.md` asks. The changeset names the right package, the right bump, and carries both declaration lines (`Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`) matching the PR body; its shape is the shipped precedent `.changeset/26475-skills-teach-queues-assignment-rules.md`. No `#NNNN` in the skills text (`check:pm-skill-id-lint` reported clean); the changeset body's `#NNNN` references are allowed there. No ceiling moves (910 of 911 tokens).

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none in the os-dev-report. The one deviation (changeset vs `skip-changeset`) is answered in ② — the PR is right; the order was not.
- `out_of_scope_findings` — `skills/objectstack-data/evals/hooks-security-seeds-datasources.json` case id 3: **confirmed, and it now contradicts this PR's text.** The eval's `expected_output` answers "A `defineDatasource` entry (`credentialsRef`, never inline credentials)" for a code datasource over a Postgres table; the rules file this PR ships now leads with the environment route for a code-declared datasource, and ADR-0015's note records that nothing mints a `sys_secret:` handle for one. The evals ship: `sync-catalog` copied 95 files, which is the 67 non-eval files plus the 28 under `evals/`, so the published bundle carries both texts. The reader who meets the contradiction is an eval grader or a skills maintainer reading the model answer, not an authoring agent following `rules/datasources.md`; the case's `must_contain` does not require `credentialsRef`, and `columnMap` / `schemaMode` it asserts are still taught. So: a follow-up card on the skills lane to re-word case 3's model answer is warranted; it is not a must-fix for this PR, whose card and claim name three texts.
- Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]` — no author note owed.
- Tier H: the PR is draft, `mergeable_state: blocked`, no auto-merge armed, no `skip-changeset` label (labels on it are the labeler's). It waits for the maintainer's own approval; this record is the review half.
- CI at the time of this read: 19 success, 13 skipped, 7 still in progress (Test Core 1/8 and 2/8, three Type Check jobs, two Lint jobs); nothing red. The landing precheck's all-green reading is the seat's to take at landing time.
- Security: no credential value, connection string or example password in the diff; variable names only. The trust consequence is a caution with no recipe in all three texts.

### ④ Design judgment

- **`skills/objectstack-data/rules/datasources.md`** against the card's acceptance ("teach exactly what landed, including the trust note", no `#NNNN`, under the ratchet) and the spec on `main`: holds. The sentence an authoring agent follows (`OS_DATASOURCE_{NAME}_PASSWORD`, switch, CLI default, precedence) is exactly `CODE_DEFINED_CREDENTIAL_ROUTE`'s prescription in `common.zod.ts` and the code behind it. Nothing undelivered is taught; the collision refusal and the unset-variable note are left to the ADR, which is right for this reader (no valid pair of names collides, and the runtime message names the variable). One optional strengthening for a later edit, not owed here: the `credentialsRef` bullet still reads as a channel a code author could pick, while a handle exists only for a datasource saved through Setup; the lead sentence already steers the reader to the environment route, and the schema does accept `credentialsRef` in every `schemaMode`, so the text is not false.
- **ADR-0015 §10 note** against its first consumer and execution plan: the consumer is `DatasourceConnectionService.connect()` as shipped on `main`; no plan is owed because the note records landed behaviour, and it says so (ruling, PR, and the `#28325` corrections named in the lede). The guards it lists are the guards the code enforces, and the "not taken" list is the implementation's own.
- **ADR-0062 D3 amendment** against the runtime it governs: the resolution order and the five conditions are the code's predicate; the pointer to ADR-0015 for the operator caution keeps the two ADRs' division of labour (binding decision in 0015, runtime decision in 0062). The declared-growth form matches the ADR's precedent.
- Nothing taught would mislead a third-party agent installing the published skills; the one contradiction it would ship is the pre-existing eval case 3, carried as a follow-up above.

No must-fix.
